item.title: Dutch housing update: money for new homes, rising interest rates
item.description:
Partner content

Dutch housing update: money for new homes, rising interest rates

September 18, 2026

There was some good news for home buyers in this week’s budget with the announcement of a massive financial package to boost new residential development. There are also signs that house price rises are slowing down, although interest rates are shooting up and the issue of foundations continues to be confusing. This and more in the latest housing news round-up.

Budget briefing

There was not much in the way of direct measures impacting on the Dutch housing market in this week’s budget. For example, the government did not announce any new changes to the current mortgage interest deduction set up, although there will be a slight rise in income tax rate in the first and second tax bands, which will have a minimal impact on your rebate.

Housing minister Elanor Boekholt-O’Sullivan did come up with a string of measures she hopes will boost supply in the rental sector and new construction, and is pressing ahead with plans to cut the property transfer tax for holiday homes and investment properties from 8% to 7%.

Most relevant for would-be home buyers? “Plenty of investment in large scale developments of new homes, so if you are looking for a new-build property, you could be lucky – although the changes will take time to filter through,” says Matthijs van der Heijden, a mortgage advisor with Expat Mortgages, which has been helping internationals buy a home for over 20 years.

The government is also putting a further €100 million into a special fund to help first-time buyers get a foot on the housing ladder.

Interest rate increases

Over the past 18 months interest rates have been pretty stable but have been trending upwards since the second quarter of the year, and are currently rising sharply as geopolitical uncertainties continue.

“We are not yet seeing these higher rates have an impact on house prices,” says Matthijs, “but there does seem to be a little bit of room for negotiation. And some buyers are able to have a second viewing of a property before they decide whether to put in a bid.

“So there is more opportunity for people who don’t want to rush into a purchase. And we have noticed that some estate agents are helping their clients to negotiate on or just under the asking price.”

The higher interest rates are also making it more important to have some savings if you are planning to buy, just to keep your costs as low as you can. “If you have €50,000 that you can put down towards the cost of your house, that means €50,000 you won’t have to borrow at well over 4% interest,” Matthijs points out.

Ask your mortgage-related questions

Expat Mortgages will be at the IamExpat Fair in Eindhoven on October 3, so come along and meet the team in person, or sign up for an online or in person webinar, such as the one on September 30. “Getting out and meeting people is a terrific experience,” says Matthijs. “The first thing we tell prospective home buyers is that they should realise it will be a very different experience than in their home countries.”

Seminars, whether online or in person, are a great way of getting direct answers to your questions and sharing your experiences with others. “We also try to focus on the more specific situations – people who have not even moved here yet, and entrepreneurs who may not have been active in the Netherlands for more than a year, when most banks want three years,” says Matthijs.

“We’ve also seen an increase in the number of PhD students wanting to buy, and banks are becoming a little bit more lenient. They used to say ‘no permanent contract, no mortgage,’ but that is changing as well.”

More homes on the market?

Despite there being room for negotiation in some parts of the market, the shortage of cheaper homes to buy is continuing, and single people or single-income families wanting to buy a home are still facing an uphill struggle. Demand continues to be very high for properties at the lower end of the market.

“Things have been very slow over the summer, but now more people are getting out there and looking,” says Matthijs. “And you can still expect to have to overbid if you are looking at cheaper properties. Much depends on what areas you are looking in as well.”

The fundamentals of foundations

Since April, banks have been taking more account of a property’s foundations when deciding whether or not to back a mortgage application. As yet, says Matthijs, there is no overall consensus about what to do if a property’s foundations are in need of urgent, or not-so-urgent, action. “It is primarily the bigger banks which have been the frontrunners on this,” says Matthijs. “It is very early days.”

“However, you can assume if the report shows there is €100,000 worth of repairs which need to be done before the house is properly stable, the banks are going to wonder how this is going to be paid. This could be done, for example, by increasing your mortgage loan – although many people are nowadays stretched to capacity because of the high house prices – or through having the savings in your bank account. One way or another, your bank will want to know if you can pay for the work.”

Are you thinking about buying a home in the Netherlands? Make an appointment to talk directly to a mortgage advisor and find out how much you can borrow.

item.title: Weekend will be mix of sun and showers, temperatures around 18C
item.description:
Weekend will be mix of sun and showers, temperatures around 18C

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Dutch meteorological institute is predicting a mix of showers and sunshine for the weekend.

There is still a chance of showers in the northeast of the country on Friday, according to KNMI but the evening will largely be dry. The afternoon temperature will remain around 18°C, with strong winds later in the evening.

On Saturday, there will be sun in the southeast but the rest of the country will see mostly cloudy skies. By the afternoon, there will be a chance of showers.

The north will see highs of 19°C while the southern part of the country will get up to 22°C.

Saturday evening will see rainstorms, including moderately strong winds along the coast.

Sunday bring more run but also more sunshine, with highs around 18°C.

item.title: Courts asked to shut 130 farms for breaching nitrogen limits
item.description:
Courts asked to shut 130 farms for breaching nitrogen limits

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Around 130 farmers risk being forced to give up their businesses after environmental group Mobilisation for the Environment (MOB) petitioned regional courts to tear up their nature permits, according to an investigation by RTL.

The organisation has started legal action in 10 provinces since 2023, asking judges to withdraw the permits of farms that exceed the limits for nitrogen depositions near Natura 2000 conservation areas.

Provincial governments have so far rejected applications from MOB, arguing that the cabinet in The Hague is working on a voluntary buyout scheme and other measures to reduce cattle numbers and nitrogen pollution.

Farmers must reduce ammonia emissions by 42% to 46% by 2035, compared to 2019 levels, under the latest package announced by agriculture minister Jaimi van Essen in June. The measures still have to be put before parliament.

The failure of successive cabinets to come up with a definitive plan since the Council of State ruled the system for issuing nature permits illegal in 2019 has prompted MOB to take the provinces to court.

Concentration in south

The majority of requests were made in the southern provinces of Noord-Brabant, Limburg, Gelderland and Overijssel, where pig, poultry and cattle farming is concentrated.

Noord-Brabant decided to withdraw its permits in July after a deadline of a year to settle the issue with MOB expired.

Van Essen said earlier this month that court orders to shut down farms were “exactly what we’re trying to prevent” with the government’s package of measures, which include a 5% to 10% across the board cut to livestock numbers as a last resort.

But Chris Backes, professor of environmental law at Utrecht University, questioned whether the plans went far enough.

“Measures by the national government are only part of the solution,” he told RTL. “For some nature areas they are sufficient, according to research by the Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency (PBL).

“But in most cases the provinces will have to implement additional measures.”

item.title: Family of man who died during arrest file manslaughter complaint
item.description:
Family of man who died during arrest file manslaughter complaint

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The family of a man who died after being arrested when police wrongly suspected him of stealing a fatbike have formally accused the force of manslaughter.

Alfredo Goeloe, 51, collapsed as officers restrained him after he was stopped on the bike in Rotterdam on Saturday evening. Police tried unsuccessfully to resuscitate him at the scene using a defibrilator.

In a video clip shot by a passer-by, Mr Goeloe could be heard screaming in pain and protesting that he had diabetes. His family said he had gone out on his sister’s fatbike to fetch diabetes medication while he was attending her baby shower party.

Around 1,000 people took part in a silent vigil on Monday evening and a march to the police station on Zuidplein.

A police spokesman later admitted that the bike had not been stolen. Mr Goeloe was pinned to the ground after he allegedly resisted arrest when police tried to detain him for failing to show ID papers.

The lawyer for the family, Gerard Roethof, said a formal complaint of manslaughter had been filed against the police force, which independent investigators will now have to assess.

“Too fast”

“The family say this is about much more than the order to use force,” Roethof told NOS. “We think this is a case of manslaughter, or in any event severe assault with fatal consequences.”

The prosecution department said on Friday that initial investigations showed he had been stopped by police on suspicion of riding too fast on the fatbike rather than because the vehicle was stolen.

At the time police in the area were looking out for a man and woman described as around 40 years old who had allegedly stolen a fatbike.

The internal police investigations division Rijksrecherche is examining the circumstances of Mr Goeloe’s death, including video footage, and the family’s complaint.

item.title: Pro-Palestinian protesters arrested at Israel event in Amsterdam
item.description:
Pro-Palestinian protesters arrested at Israel event in Amsterdam

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Around 45 pro-Palestinian protesters have been arrested after they disrupted a demonstration by supporters of Israel in Amsterdam.

Police led members of the group away after they sprayed slogans in red paint on the ground in Dam Square, near the national war memorial, where a group of several hundred had gathered for an event organised by Christians for Israel.

Speakers at the event included Chris Stoffer, leader of the orthodox Protestant party SGP, and the Dutch chief rabbi Binyamin Jacobs.

Earlier in the day the group Amsterdam Palestina Coalitie lost a court case in which it tried to overturn a ban by the city council on a counter-demonstration in Dam Square.

A spokesman for mayor Femke Halsema said there was a risk of public disorder if the both groups were allowed to demonstrate in the same place.

Pro-Palestinian protesters who went to the square in spite of the ban were arrested. A giant Palestinian flag that was hung from the upper floors of the H&M store overlooking the monument was removed by police.

The counter-demonstration was moved to Oude Turfmarkt, around 500 metres away on Rokin.

The public prosecution service will now decide whether to bring charges against the protesters in the square.

item.title: Sauna wrong to toss out woman wearing a burkini
item.description:
Sauna wrong to toss out woman wearing a burkini

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A dress code banning burkinis from saunas is discriminatory, judges at the Dutch human rights institute have concluded.

The Zwaluwhoeve sauna in Hierden removed a young woman from the facility for wearing a burkini, a body and head-covering swimsuit, citing hygiene reasons.

The center “insufficiently substantiated that wearing a burkini poses health or safety risks,” wrote in its decision on Thursday.

The woman was visiting the sauna in June 2025 with her family, on a day when bathing suits were mandatory.

After enjoying the wellness space for four hours, she was approached by an employee and told to leave. The women left and later filed a claim at the the Netherlands Institute for Human Rights.

According to Zwaluwhoeve’s dress code, burkinis are not allowed.

“Studies indicate that there is no difference in hygiene between different types of clothing made of swimwear fabric,” the court ruled, noting that other saunas in the Netherlands permit burkinis.

The dress code, the judges concluded, is discriminatory on both religious and gender grounds.

item.title: Schreuder calls Europa League “tough” after 5-0 loss to Juventus
item.description:
Schreuder calls Europa League “tough” after 5-0 loss to Juventus

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

NEC coach Dick Schreuder admitted his team was struggling to find the right blend after the Nijmegen club crashed to a 5-0 Europa League defeat against Italian club Juventus.

“I don’t see any uncertainty in the squad, but the new players are having a tough time,” Schreuder told Omroep Gelderland following Thursday night’s match in Turin.

“They haven’t had time to develop, they’ve had to be ready for European football right away when some of them are already finding the Eredivisie challenging. They’ve came from the under-21s or the Danish second tier.”

NEC have had to rebuild since losing several key players in the summer transfer window, including midfielders Kodai Sano and Sami Ouaissa to PSV. Their star recruit was former Ajax midfielder Dusan Tadic, who will be 38 in November.

They also took the field in Italy with a stand-in goalkeeper, Nikolas Polster, after Gonzalo Crettaz was sent off in the last European match against Bødo/Glimt.

Polster was at fault for the first two Juventus goals, before the match was ended as a contest 10 minutes before half-time when Nick Woltemade scored from the penalty spot after Almugera Kabar clearly fouled Nico González.

Juve strolled through the second half, adding two goals in the last 15 minutes to complete a humbling night for NEC.

Their next Europa League match is at home to Bulgarian club Levski Sofia on October 15.

item.title: Arrests after rioters at anti-asylum protest clash with police
item.description:
Arrests after rioters at anti-asylum protest clash with police

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

At least 10 people have been arrested after riot police once again broke up a violent demonstration against plans to open an asylum seekers’ centre.

Around 300 people turned up to protest at the council building in Opleusden, Gelderland, where Neder-Betuwe municipal councillors were discussing where to house 132 refugees, including eight unaccompanied minors, on Thursday evening.

The demonstration was initially peaceful, but riot police were sent in after some protesters began attacking officers when the crowd was asked to disperse at around 10.30pm.

Flares were lit, buildings were vandalised and kerbstones were ripped out of the ground to throw at police. No injuries were reported.

A group calling itself Defend Rivierlanden announced the demonstration in advance.

“Defend” groups have been implicated in violent anti-asylum protests in towns and villages across the Netherlands this summer, including Loosduinen and Engelen.

They were also prominent during the riots in The Hague last September in which around 1,200 demonstrators clashed with police and the offices of political party D66, led by the now prime minister Rob Jetten, were vandalised.

The mayor of Neder-Betuwe, Jan Kottelenberg, said he did not expect a major confrontation because the municipality has not yet specified where the refugees should be housed.

He added that extra police were not drafted in for the meeting because capacity was already stretched by the need for extra patrols in nearby Overasselt, the village where a group of armed men laid siege to a farmhouse three weeks ago.

item.title: Power bank that ignited on KLM flight belonged to former CEO
item.description:
Power bank that ignited on KLM flight belonged to former CEO

September 18, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The power bank that ignited on a KLM flight en route to Curaçao, forcing the plane to return to Schiphol, belonged to the airline’s former CEO, according to NU.nl.

Multiple sources tell news website that the electronic device belonged to Camiel Eurlings, who was charging contrary to safety rules while traveling in first class on the flight to Willemstad.

Witnesses said that Eurlings was asleep at the time and was awoken by a bang when the power bank exploded.

KLM would not confirm the reporting, citing privacy concerns.

Flight KL735 was five and a half hours into its trip when the electronic device started emitting smoke. A photo obtained by RTL shows shattered window screen and burn debris.

Crew members were able to extinguish the fire. KLM said that one person was slightly injured but would not confirm if it was Eurlings.

The ex-topman celebrated his 53rd birthday on Wednesday. He joined KLM in 2011, first as corporate director and later as CEO.

After leaving the company in 2014, he joined the Dutch Olympic committee. He was forced to resign after Quote magazine revealed his ex-girlfriend had filed a police report allegedly that Eurlings had assaulted her.

Prior to working at KLM, Eurlings had a long career as a CDA politician. He served as a member of parliament, a member of European parliament and has transportation minister.

This is the second time a KLM flight has been disrupted because of an incident with a powerbank. In August 2025, a device in an overhead storage bin caught fire during a flight to São Paulo, Brazil.

That flight was also forced backed to Amsterdam after the cabin filled with smoke. According to KLM, it was the first time a flight had been disrupted by a power bank catching fire.

Airlines have special rules for powerbanks to reduce the fire risk. Passengers may only bring two on board, with a capacity of 100 Wh or less. KLM bans travellers from storing powerbanks in the overhead bins and from charging them on board.

item.title: Jetten refuses to pick a side as opposition warns of drama
item.description:
Jetten refuses to pick a side as opposition warns of drama

September 17, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten has declined to say whether his minority coalition will seek support from the left or right to pass its first budget, telling MPs on the second day of debates that making that choice now would be “short-changing the country”.

Instead of committing one way or the other, Jetten said the cabinet would send invitations on Thursday evening to seven opposition parties – Pro, JA21, ChristenUnie, SGP, BBB, Volt and 50PLUS – for a new round of talks on support for the current budget and tax plan.

But the two parties whose votes matter most, which are pulling left and right, have said they see little point in such talks. Opposition party Pro leader Jesse Klaver said more discussions would be a repeat of the ones that collapsed in the summer.

Far-right JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said the cabinet had to choose. “Broad isn’t going to work,” he told Jetten. “Which way are you going?”

Jetten admitted the cabinet had underestimated how much time it needed in August to work opposition demands into the budget, and said it wanted to keep talking in the coming weeks. He again said a broad agreement was his preference, but did not rule out seeking support for individual budgets if needed.

“A drama for the Netherlands”
Klaver said the coalition is “divided to the bone”, and told Jetten “lock yourself in a room,” because “if you don’t make the choice, it will grind to a halt and this autumn will be a drama for the Netherlands.”

ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker said it was “hard for us to talk” to a cabinet that could not agree with itself.

On the first day of the debates yesterday, Eerdmans said a total deal with the cabinet was no longer realistic and JA21 would judge each departmental budget separately, ruling out support for the climate budget and probably the asylum budget so long as the spreading law for asylum seekers remains in force.

Klaver responded that Pro would withhold support from every budget if the cabinet struck separate deals with JA21. The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA has 66 of the 150 seats in parliament and needs 16 extra votes in the senate.

Siding with Pro would give it the easiest chance of a majority, but the right-wing VVD does not want to concede to them on many issues.

Stabs in the back
PVV leader Geert Wilders opened the day by confronting Jetten with an article in the newspaper AD, in which unnamed ministers criticised the prime minister for failing to take charge, one saying the only direction he took was the visual direction””, managing the image.

Wilders said Jetten’s colleagues had “stuck three daggers in your back” and asked what he thought of not being trusted by his own party.

Jetten said he was proud of his team and “we are making the best of it”.

Tax plans
In mid-November parliament will vote on the tax plan. Pro and ChristenUnie have both said they will not back it as it stands, because the burden falls largely on people in work, and Eerdmans said there is no way the plan can satisfy both JA21 and Pro at the same time.

The Council of State, the government’s main advisory body, said this week that €5.8 billion of the €6 billion in tax rises planned for 2027 would be paid by workers, while the burden on companies and wealth falls slightly. A decision on the tax on savings and investments, known as Box 3, has been postponed until next year.

Jetten said the cabinet would spend an extra €10 billion on infrastructure in the coming years and told Pro that the nitrogen plans would not be watered down, though “improvements” were possible provided they delivered the same reduction in emissions.

MPs will vote on motions, including a motion of no confidence tabled by Wilders, at the end of the debate on Thursday night.
